root_causes.name: Active transactions (excluding monitoring user)
root_causes.description: All currently open / in-flight user transactions on the instance, excluding the dbdome monitoring login (dbd_mon_usr / dbdome_mon_usr). Surfaces who is holding a transaction, against which database, for how long, the transaction state and the SQL text - for spotting long-running or abandoned transactions, blocking, and anomalous activity.
root_causes.resolution: Review long-running or abandoned transactions: identify the session/login, database, duration and SQL text; chase blocking chains and transactions open beyond expected thresholds. Persistent open transactions from application logins may indicate a missing COMMIT/ROLLBACK.

expected.description: Open user transactions are present (excluding the monitoring account)

detect.sqlserver:
SELECT
    @@SERVERNAME AS server,
    s.session_id,
    s.login_name,
    s.host_name,
    s.program_name,
    DB_NAME(s.database_id) AS database_name,
    t.transaction_id,
    tat.transaction_begin_time,
    DATEDIFF(SECOND, tat.transaction_begin_time, GETDATE()) AS duration_seconds,
    tat.transaction_state,
    SUBSTRING(st.text, 1, 4000) AS query_text
FROM sys.dm_tran_active_transactions tat
JOIN sys.dm_tran_session_transactions t ON t.transaction_id = tat.transaction_id
JOIN sys.dm_exec_sessions s ON s.session_id = t.session_id
LEFT JOIN sys.dm_exec_connections c ON c.session_id = s.session_id
OUTER APPLY sys.dm_exec_sql_text(c.most_recent_sql_handle) st
WHERE s.is_user_process = 1
  AND s.login_name NOT IN ('dbd_mon_usr','dbdome_mon_usr')
ORDER BY tat.transaction_begin_time
